allowance(address,address).details: Returns the remaining number of tokens that `spender` will be allowed to spend on behalf of `owner` through {transferFrom}. This is zero by default. This value changes when {approve} or {transferFrom} are called.

approve(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-approve}. NOTE: If `value` is the maximum `uint256`, the allowance is not updated on `transferFrom`. This is semantically equivalent to an infinite approval. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

authorize(uint256,uint256,uint256).details: Official swaps: each direction on its own. The PoolManager keeps every caller's deltas apart, so two      executors in one unlock settle opposite swaps with separate transfers. A swap pays the fee, so whatever it      leaves unused cannot make another pool cheaper than the official one.

authorizeLiquidity(uint256,uint256).details: Official liquidity: only the net of the transaction. Liquidity moves without a fee, so adding and removing      the same amount in one transaction must leave nothing a transfer for another pool could use (review R-02).

balanceOf(address).details: Returns the value of tokens owned by `account`.

params.nonce: makes `proofDigest(msg.sender, keep, other, nonce)` start with PROOF_BITS zero bits. It binds only        the caller, the two ids and the nonce, never the chain head, so nobody can invalidate it by composing first.

decimals().details: Returns the number of decimals used to get its user representation. For example, if `decimals` equals `2`, a balance of `505` tokens should be displayed to a user as `5.05` (`505 / 10 ** 2`). Tokens usually opt for a value of 18, imitating the relationship between Ether and Wei. This is the default value returned by this function, unless it's overridden. NOTE: This information is only used for _display_ purposes: it in no way affects any of the arithmetic of the contract, including {IERC20-balanceOf} and {IERC20-transfer}.

name().details: Returns the name of the token.

symbol().details: Returns the symbol of the token, usually a shorter version of the name.

totalSupply().details: Returns the value of tokens in existence.

transfer(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transfer}. Requirements: - `to` cannot be the zero address. - the caller must have a balance of at least `value`.

transferFrom(address,address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transferFrom}. Skips emitting an {Approval} event indicating an allowance update. This is not required by the ERC. See {xref-ERC20-_approve-address-address-uint256-bool-}[_approve]. NOTE: Does not update the allowance if the current allowance is the maximum `uint256`. Requirements: - `from` and `to` cannot be the zero address. - `from` must have a balance of at least `value`. - the caller must have allowance for ``from``'s tokens of at least `value`.

BLOCKS_SHA256().notice: sha256 of the 10,000 Bitcoin block hashes the masks come from (provenance, see data/README.md).

MASKS_SHA256().notice: sha256 of the 10,000 part masks (data/computed/masks.bin), derived from Bitcoin blocks 0..9,999.

MAX_WALK().notice: Steps along a slot's dealing order before ranking the ids left by their fixed per-id scores (bounds a         reveal when the pool holds very few ids; with a few hundred ids or more the walk practically never gets there).

PROOF_BITS().notice: Leading zero bits of the light proof: about a second in a browser. A ritual, not a security measure.

PROTECTION().notice: Launch protection: how long, and what one address may receive in that time (2% of the supply).

accruedX18(address).notice: UNI x1e18 credited to `account` but not claimed yet (whole wei and dust).

cardWeight(uint8,uint8).notice: Weight of a card: parts × (1 + 2% per extra layer + 5% when complete), in W1 units.

chainHead().notice: Head of the compose chain; starts at the provenance of the Bitcoin blocks.

commitmentOf(uint256).notice: Provenance commitment: a fragment commits to its block (via the provenance root), id and parts; a work         to the SHA-256 chain of its composes.

compose(uint256,uint256,uint256).notice: Compose two of your cards with disjoint parts. `keep` survives (its ground stays), `other` is retired.

deployer().notice: The graph deployer (the Programmable Graph Factory); it alone calls `initialize`, once.

description().notice: Coin metadata, read the way Programmable reads its own coins (FoundationTokenV1: `description`,         `website`, `image`, `extraData`, `metadata()` and `metadataHash()`). Fixed forever; the launch metadata         submitted with the launch carries the same values (`launch/lint.py` checks them).

detailsOf(uint256).notice: The card's eight 32-bit part details (pixel micro-variation of art v7; not a metadata attribute).

drawCreditOf(address).notice: Tokens (wei) bought in the official pool that have not opened a slot yet.

earned(address).notice: UNI (wei) the account can claim now, exact.

fulfill(uint64,bytes32,uint256).notice: Reveal up to `max` slots of `round` in creation order with the round's verified randomness.

initialize(address,address,address,addre.notice: Wire the graph and mint the whole supply to the launch initializer. Deployer only, once.         The beacon and the mirror are deployed before the launch for this token's predicted address: a missing         one or one bound to another address reverts the whole launch.

lastBlockOf(uint64).notice: Block of the last slot opened for a round (the fallback reveal uses the hash of the next block).

metadata().notice: (description, website, image, extraData), as FoundationTokenV1 returns them.

metadataHash().notice: keccak256 of the ABI-encoded launch tuple (name, symbol, description, image, website, extraData).

notifyReward(uint256).notice: Stream `amount` UNI to the holders over one day, together with what is still streaming and the carry.

optIn().notice: Contracts (Safe, …) hold cards without weight until they opt in. Accounts without code and EIP-7702         accounts are weighted automatically.

originalMask(uint256).notice: The parts id `id` was measured with from its Bitcoin block (never changes).

outFirstOf(address).notice: The cards `setOutFirst` still sends first, in leave order (the sell helper shows and clears leftovers).

proofDigest(address,uint256,uint256,uint.notice: The light proof digest the browser searches a nonce for.

protectedUntil().notice: End of launch protection, set by the hook when the pool is created (shares a slot read on every transfer).

pruneSlots(uint256).notice: Anyone: move the reveal queue past up to `max` cancelled slots at its head. A reveal walks past cancelled         slots before the next live one; a long run of them is cleared here in parts, each call bounded.

receivedDuringProtection(address).notice: Tokens (wei) each address received during launch protection.

retiredInto(uint256).notice: A retired id points to the work it was composed into.

revoke(address).notice: Anyone: remove the automatic weight of an account that has code now (not EIP-7702) and never opted in.         Such an account had no code when it first received a unit, e.g. a pair created later at an address         someone sent a card to in advance. Its accrued UNI stays claimable; it can still `optIn()` itself.

setGuard(bool).notice: Protect your composed works: while on, a transfer that would send one of them back to the pool reverts.

setOutFirst(uint32[]).notice: Cards to send first on the next transfers out (the sell helper sets this before selling).

settleClaim(address).notice: Settle `account` and hand its whole-wei balance to the distributor to pay; the dust stays accrued.

startProtection().notice: Start launch protection; the hook calls this when the official pool is created, once.

undistributedX18().notice: UNI x1e18 not yet credited to anyone: the rest of the stream, the carry and the undivided remainder.

@dev Continue the slot's fixed order after its MAX_WALK prefix: independent per-id hash scores, then id to
      break a tie. Scores do not depend on poolCount or other ids, so adding an id can only retain the previous
      winner or select that added id, including a transition back into the prefix. Fixed pools are uniform up
      to negligible 256-bit hash collisions. Read 40 bitmap words and score only their free ids (at most 8,976
      after a missed prefix). The pool is never empty when a slot is revealed (pool >= pending slots).

@title UN1Token
 @notice 10,000 tokens. Every whole token is one unit: a card (an id #1..#10,000), a pending slot, or a naked token.
  PoolManager gate (rule ②): tokens may enter or leave the PoolManager only against an allowance the official hook
  grants inside the same transaction, for the exact amounts it moves. Only official-pool buys grant a draw (rule ①):
  units arriving under it open pending slots, revealed later from drand. Everything else moves existing units.
  Draw credit: what an account bought in the official pool and has not turned into slots yet. A slot opens when a buy
  makes the receiver cross a whole token and the credit holds a whole token; otherwise the new unit is naked. So every
  draw is backed by a whole token bought in the official pool (buying it in several parts works), and selling a
  fraction of a card's token then buying the fraction back does not draw again.
  Units leave an account in this order: a card named by the ERC721 mirror, pending slots, naked tokens, then cards:
  first those named by `setOutFirst`, then by priority (single-part fragments first, composed works last). When a transfer makes the
  receiver cross whole tokens, the first units leaving go to it; the others dissolve: pending slots are cancelled
  and cards return to the pool (superposition: appearance cleared, a composed work falls back to its own parts).
  An account can turn on `setGuard`: then a transfer that would send one of its composed works back to the pool
  reverts (moving a work to another holder, e.g. through the mirror, still works).
  Compose: two cards of the same holder with disjoint parts become one. The holder picks the id to keep; the other is
  retired forever and one token is burned. Appearances are kept and locked, layers add up, and every compose wraps
  one more SHA-256 around the provenance and appends it to the chain. One-way: a work cannot be split.
  Any address but the PoolManager can hold cards. Weight counts automatically for accounts without code and EIP-7702
  accounts; other contracts call `optIn()`. An address that had no code when it first received a unit and has code
  now (a pair or wallet deployed later at a precomputed address) loses that automatic weight through `revoke`.
  Launch protection (with the hook): for 5 minutes after the pool is created, an address may receive at most 2% of
  the supply in total, from any sender other than itself; sending tokens away does not give room back. Transfers
  into the PoolManager are not counted.
  Fee distribution (exact, no external calls): the distributor streams each UNI deposit linearly over one day. A
  global accumulator (UNI x1e18 per weight unit) advances with time; every account is settled right before its weight
  changes. Remainders are carried, never dropped: time with no weight is re-streamed with the next deposit, division
  remainders roll into the next update, and accounts accrue in UNI x1e18 so claims lose no dust. Buying and selling
  in the same block earns nothing: time does not move.
